promptText: When an owner wants a collection or soft-brand option for a hotel conversion in Mexico, which brands are commonly considered?
rawResponse:
When an owner in Mexico is considering a hotel conversion and seeks a *soft‑brand* or *collection* option, several well-established franchise groups and their flexible “soft brand” portfolios are commonly considered:

1. **Marriott International**  
   - They offer multiple soft brands suitable for conversions with minimal impact on a property's existing identity:
     - **The Luxury Collection** – typically for grand, historic & luxury properties ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriott_International?utm_source=openai)).
     - **Autograph Collection** – upscale/upper‑upscale independent-style hotels where the original name and character may be preserved ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autograph_Collection?utm_source=openai)).
     - **Tribute Portfolio** – targets lifestyle-independent properties that don’t meet Autograph’s entry thresholds ([hospitality.today](https://www.hospitality.today/article/marriotts-soft-brands-are-a-distribution-strategy-not-a-brand-strategy?utm_source=openai)).
     - **Design Hotels** – design-forward soft brand, often heritage or architecturally unique, inherited within Marriott’s portfolio ([hospitality.today](https://www.hospitality.today/article/marriotts-soft-brands-are-a-distribution-strategy-not-a-brand-strategy?utm_source=openai)).

2. **Hilton**  
   - **Curio Collection** – for distinctive, upscale properties maintaining their local identity while benefiting from Hilton’s reservation and loyalty platforms ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)).
   - **Tapestry Collection** – similar positioning but generally slightly more accessible in standards than Curio ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai)).

3. **Hyatt**  
   - **Unbound Collection** – lifestyle and boutique properties seeking brand affiliation while maintaining autonomy ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai)).
   - **JdV by Hyatt** – another option, especially in some markets looking for conversion flexibility ([hospitality.today](https://www.hospitality.today/article/marriotts-soft-brands-are-a-distribution-strategy-not-a-brand-strategy?utm_source=openai)).

4. **Choice Hotels**  
   - **Ascend Collection** – often regarded as the industry’s first soft brand (launched in 2008), targeting historic or boutique upscale hotels ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascend_Collection?utm_source=openai)).

5. **Wyndham**  
   - **Trademark Hotel Collection** – focuses on upscale properties that want to retain some individuality ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai)).
   - **Registry Collection** – positioned at a higher end than Trademark, still under the soft-brand conversion model ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)).

6. **IHG (InterContinental Hotels Group)**  
   - **Vignette Collection** – aimed at upscale to upper‑upscale conversions, encouraging flexibility in branding and design ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)).

7. **Accor**  
   - Offers soft‑brand or conversion‑friendly options like **MGallery Collection**, **Emblems**, and **Handwritten Collection** (the latter aimed at flexible conversions) ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai)).

8. **Preferred Hotels & Resorts** and other independent collections  
   - **Preferred Hotels & Resorts**, **Leading Hotels of the World**, and **Small Luxury Hotels of the World** (SLH) are independent soft brand systems that aggregate boutique and luxury properties without strict uniformity—valuable for owners prioritizing design, heritage, and autonomy ([hotelmanagement.net](https://www.hotelmanagement.net/own/soft-brand-collections-new-norm?utm_source=openai)).

9. **Regional / Specialty Options**  
   - In Mexico, **Gamma by Posadas** (a soft-brand style approach) stands out as a local option within the Posadas group ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai)).
   - **Spark by Hilton**, although not strictly a soft‑brand, was launched in Mexico in early 2025 specifically for midscale conversion projects and could be relevant depending on property level and owner objectives ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spark_by_Hilton?utm_source=openai)).

---

**Summary Table (for quick reference):**

- **Marriott**: The Luxury Collection; Autograph Collection; Tribute Portfolio; Design Hotels  
- **Hilton**: Curio Collection; Tapestry Collection; Spark (conversion-focused midscale)  
- **Hyatt**: Unbound Collection; JdV by Hyatt  
- **Choice**: Ascend Collection  
- **Wyndham**: Trademark Collection; Registry Collection  
- **IHG**: Vignette Collection  
- **Accor**: MGallery, Emblems, Handwritten Collection  
- **Independent**: Preferred Hotels & Resorts; Leading Hotels of the World; Small Luxury Hotels  
- **Local**: Gamma by Posadas (Mexico)  

These soft-brand options allow owners in Mexico converting existing hotels to partner with major chains or independent collections, gain broader distribution channels and loyalty program access, while maintaining the hotel's distinct identity and cultural appeal.
